Resolves #20054

`DomAccessCanvasTransfer.spec` now gives `Neo.main.DomAccess` back right after it imports the real singleton. A later spec in the same worker gets setup's stub again instead of a main-thread `DomAccess` over a `document` it does not have.

The arms call the imported instance, and the production path under test reads `Neo.worker.Manager`, so nothing needs the namespace entry after the import. The restore sits next to the `document` restore that was already there. Hooks would not work here: under `fullyParallel` a file-level `afterAll` can run between this file's tests in one worker, while the import runs once.

Evidence: L2 (unit, CI) → L2 required (test isolation only). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Local paired run (`DomAccessCanvasTransfer.spec` + `GalleryInternalId.spec`, `--workers=1`): 1 failed on `dev` `e2f77dd0fb`, 7/7 at head over three runs. Without the restore line the file is `dev`'s. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the spec's own arms; locally 20/20 over `--repeat-each=5`. |

## Deltas from ticket
- The restore runs at module level instead of in an `afterAll`, for the `fullyParallel` reason above.
- I also paired all seven specs that import the real `DomAccess` with `GalleryInternalId.spec` in one worker: 66/66 at head.
